research_rationale:
basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search. EO 10253 (signed 1951-06-11; 16 FR 5605; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10253.txt, read in full) directs the Director of the Bureau of the Budget (now of the Office of Management and Budget) to develop programs and issue regulations and orders for improved federal statistical work, to study and assist agency statistical work, and sets objectives, consultation and signing rules. Identity: the Title 3 heading of Executive Order 10253 of June 11, 1951, providing for the improvement of the work of Federal executive agencies with respect to statistical information at 16 FR 5605, the title and the date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory splits section 2 into fragments, repeats one, omits the recital, section 3 and section 7 and runs section 6 through unrelated Federal Register pages and the next document, so I replaced it with eight clauses (inventory override): the authority recital and sections 1 to 7; the held text interleaves section 7 and the signature after the issue's contents pages, which I read through. Own terms: no section has an end date or ending condition; the amendments of EO 12013 and EO 12318 substitute officers and, for section 7, replace the text, and are recorded as later events, none of them revoking the order or ending a section. Later instruments: a search of every held order text for the number 10253 finds EO 12013 section 2 (amends sections 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 and adds section 8), EO 12318 section 2 (further amends the same sections, replaces section 7 and revokes section 8) and, in EO 12318 section 4(a), a revocation of EO 12013 itself, which does not reinstate or revoke anything in this order beyond the amendments EO 12318 restates; the order's own copy, the 1989 codification snapshot and Federal Register and CFR texts that cite it as authority are not instruments affecting it. EO 12318 recites the date of this order as July 11, 1951; the number and the sections amended identify the order. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes, carry no coverage warning, and record 13, 13 and 3 hits for the order number respectively. Limit stated plainly: the continuing predicate rests on the held original text, the held amendments and the bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09); 31 U.S.C. 1104(d), the statutory successor of the section the order cites, is held and still directs the statistical programs, but the held text does not show how the Office of Management and Budget now exercises the functions, and the original of section 7 is gone from the current text.

EO 12013 and EO 12318 amend sections 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 (and EO 12013 adds, and EO 12318 revokes, a section 8 that is not part of the original inventory); none revokes or supersedes the order, and no other held order text, statute text or search result does.","independent_command_check":"Section 1 (the programs, regulations and orders), section 2 (continuing study), section 3 (objectives), section 4 (signing and binding force), section 5 (consultation), section 6 (additional authority and precedence) and section 7 (as amended, redelegation to the Administrator for the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs) are separate; none was found ended.","savings_check":"The order has no savings or transition clause; EO 12013 and EO 12318 each provide that actions taken under the transferred functions remain in effect, which concerns those orders' transfers and not an end of this order.","scope_check":"The corrected inventory has eight clauses covering the whole order: the authority recital and sections 1 to 7."}
